CPGRAMS Grievance Redressal Framework: The Centralised Public Grievance Redress and Monitoring System (CPGRAMS) is an official 24x7 web platform for citizens to lodge complaints regarding public services, civic deficiencies, utility breakdowns, and administrative malpractices across municipal and governmental bodies. Every registered grievance receives a unique tracking number, an assigned nodal officer, and a strict resolution timeframe defined under the Citizen Charter.

How to File an Effective Grievance: When submitting a public complaint, citizens should clearly provide: (1) Exact physical location and nearest landmark, (2) Nature and duration of the problem, (3) Number of affected residents or households, (4) Specific public hazard or risk involved, (5) Previous complaint or token reference numbers if any. Clear, factual descriptions ensure rapid categorization and nodal officer dispatch without back-and-forth inquiries.

Water Supply Grievances & Redressal Rules: Jurisdiction covers drinking water shortages, contaminated tap water, pipeline bursts, broken valves, low pressure, and emergency water tanker dispatch. Handled by the municipal Jal Board / Jal Sansthan. Standard Resolution SLA: Emergency water pipeline bursts and acute contamination must be inspected within 12 hours and resolved within 24 hours. Tanker requests must be attended within 4 hours.

Electricity & Power Infrastructure Redressal Rules: Jurisdiction covers transformer blowouts, fallen or sparking electrical wires, prolonged unannounced power outages, low-voltage fluctuations damaging appliances, and billing inaccuracies. Handled by the State Power Distribution Company (DISCOM). Standard Resolution SLA: Live wire hazards and transformer breakdowns must be addressed within 12 to 24 hours. Billing disputes are resolved within 7 business days.

Police & Law and Order Grievances: Jurisdiction covers refusal by local police station to register an FIR, non-investigation of missing persons or theft, local patrol inadequacy, anti-social nuisance, and police misconduct. Complaints are triaged to the Superintendent of Police (Law & Grievance Cell). Standard Resolution SLA: Urgent law-and-order threats and missing person alerts are escalated within 12 hours.

Sanitation, Waste Management & Health Hazards: Jurisdiction covers overflowing community garbage bins, irregular municipal waste collection, open sewer line blockages, street sweeping neglect, dead animal removal, and stagnant water causing mosquito-borne disease outbreaks (Dengue/Malaria). Handled by the Chief Municipal Health Officer and Swachh Bharat Cell. Standard Resolution SLA: 24 hours for garbage lifting and drain unblocking; 6 hours for animal carcass removal.

Roads, Pavements & Public Infrastructure: Jurisdiction covers dangerous potholes, collapsed road culverts, damaged footpaths, illegal speed breakers, missing manhole covers, and malfunctioning street lights. Handled by the Public Works Department (PWD), Municipal Corporation, and National Highways Authority (NHAI). Standard Resolution SLA: Missing manhole covers within 12 hours; road pothole patch repairs within 48 hours.

Healthcare, Dispensaries & Public Hospitals: Jurisdiction covers non-availability of essential medicines at government dispensaries, absent medical officers, denial of emergency medical treatment, dilapidated primary health centres, and ambulance delays. Handled by the Chief Medical Officer (CMO) and Directorate of Health Services. Standard Resolution SLA: Immediate 12 hours for critical healthcare denial; 48 hours for facility supplies.

Ration & Public Distribution System (PDS): Jurisdiction covers Fair Price Shop dealers denying mandated food grain rations, black-marketing of subsidized goods, biometric authentication failures, overcharging, and delays in issuing ration cards. Handled by the District Supply Officer (DSO) under the National Food Security Act. Standard Resolution SLA: 36 hours for dealership inspection; 7 days for card correction.

Pension, EPFO & Provident Fund Redressal: Jurisdiction covers delayed pension disbursement, incorrect Pension Payment Order (PPO) calculations, delayed EPF provident fund claim settlements, non-transfer of provident funds, and pension arrears. Handled by the Regional Provident Fund Commissioner (EPFO) and Department of Pension & Pensioners Welfare. Standard Resolution SLA: 48 hours to acknowledge; full settlement within 15 days.

Land Records, Revenue & Public Encroachment: Jurisdiction covers delayed land mutation (dakhil kharij), non-issuance of Khasra/Khatauni land records, patwari harassment, illegal land grabbing of public parks and common land. Handled by the Sub-Divisional Magistrate (SDM Revenue) and District Magistrate. Standard Resolution SLA: Encroachment stop-work notice within 48 hours; land record correction within 96 hours.

Municipal Certificates & Civil Registrations: Jurisdiction covers delayed birth and death certificates, property tax assessment errors, trade license issuance harassment, and municipal building plan approvals. Handled by the Municipal Registrar and e-District Citizen Facilitation Centers. Standard Resolution SLA: 48 hours for standard certificates; 7 days for building inspection reports.

Education, Samagra Shiksha & Public Schools: Jurisdiction covers teacher absenteeism in government schools, sub-standard mid-day meal quality, lack of functional drinking water and toilets for students, refusal of RTE (Right to Education) admissions, and school safety hazards. Handled by the District Education Officer (DEO). Standard Resolution SLA: 72 hours for school inspections.

Anti-Corruption & Vigilance Redressal: Jurisdiction covers demands for illegal gratification/bribes by government functionaries, extortion, fund embezzlement, and tender manipulation. Handled by the Vigilance Officer, Anti-Corruption Bureau (ACB), and State Lokayukta. Standard Resolution SLA: Preliminary vigilance inquiry initiated within 24 hours with strict whistleblower confidentiality.

Citizen Escalation Hierarchy & Redressal Appeals: If a grievance is not resolved within the prescribed Citizen Charter SLA deadline, or if the citizen is dissatisfied with the nodal officer response, the portal provides a 3-tier escalation mechanism: (1) Tier 1: Nodal Redressal Officer (Initial resolution), (2) Tier 2: First Appellate Authority (Senior Departmental Secretary/Joint Commissioner), (3) Tier 3: Central Administrative Oversight & Lokayukta. Citizens have the legal right to reopen closed grievances within 30 days if unsatisfied.

Matters Excluded & Ineligible under Grievance Portal: The grievance portal does NOT entertain: (1) Sub-judice matters currently pending trial before any Court of Law, (2) Personal or family civil disputes between private citizens, (3) Right to Information (RTI) inquiries (which must be filed separately under the RTI Act, 2005), (4) Anonymous or pseudonymous complaints lacking actionable facts, (5) Religious or political propaganda.
